newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Khieu Samphan favoured front man of Khmer Rouge.
newsitem.headline: Khieu Samphan favoured front man of Khmer Rouge.

text.p: Khmer Rouge nominal leader Khieu Samphan has for years served as the more presentable public face of the reviled guerrilla movement in Cambodia.
Officially called the president of the movement's provisional government, Khieu Samphan has now reportedly been abducted by his own leader, notorious Khmer Rouge strongman Pol Pot.

Cambodia's deputy chief of general staff Nhiek Bun Chhay told reporters that Pol Pot took three top officials, including Khieu Samphan, as hostages when he fled his northern stronghold of Anlong Veng last week.

He said Pol Pot was now holed up in the jungle about 20 km (12 miles) east of Anlong Veng in rough jungle terrain with 250 to 300 fighters and their families. About 1,000 breakaway rebels were surrounding Pol Pot's position, he said.

The reports have not been independently confirmed and some observers were sceptical of the reports of fighting between Pol Pot's followers and breakaway Khmer Rouge rebels as well as the hostage-taking.

Some political analysts and observers have expressed doubt that Khieu Samphan, who along with Pol Pot was a principal architect of the 1975-1979 "killing fields" regime, was being held against his will.
The dapper, silver-haired man of 65, has been extremely close to Pol Pot over the years.

Described by scholars as a somber, austere and extremely disciplined man, Khieu Samphan was a classmate of Pol Pot and other future Khmer Rouge guerrillas in France in the 1950s and returned to Cambodia to become a teacher and then a newspaper editor.
King Norodom Sihanouk, then the national leader, closed down the left-wing newspaper and Khieu Samphan was beaten, stripped naked and jailed for two months without charges.

After a stint in politics under Sihanouk's rule, he left Phnom Penh and climbed the ranks of the Khmer Rouge, becoming commander-in-chief of the guerrilla army that seized power in April 1975. He served as head of state under the regime.
After the Khmer Rouge was ousted in 1979, Khieu Samphan led the Khmer Rouge's diplomatic effort to rehabilitate itself.
Some one million people are believed to have been killed through executions, starvation, hard labour and disease during the Khmer Rouge's rule.
As a more acceptable public face than Pol Pot, he became president of the Khmer Rouge's provisional government and returned to Phnom Penh after the guerrillas signing a 1991 peace pact.
He was beaten by an angry mob, suggesting Cambodians perhaps did not distinguish him from Brother Number One, Pol Pot.

More recently Khieu Samphan has once again tried his hand at returning to the mainstream. He announced over rebel radio that he intended to form a political alliance with co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh, who has welcomed his support.
